## Connection settings

*Configure → Connection settings*

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Enable live map** | Enable the live cleaning map for robots with position sensing (Roomba 900, i, s, j, Braava m). |
| **Ask the robot for its position** | Only offered for robots that do not report their position on their own. Asks the robot about once a second while it cleans, to draw the cleaning path live. Off: the map shows the last finished mission from the iRobot cloud instead, if cloud access is set up. |
| **Align the path with the rooms** | Only with the option above. Turns the cleaning path against the floor plan until it lies on its rooms. Room tracking uses the same turned positions, so a wrong angle also names the wrong room. Not the same as “Rotate the map picture”, which turns the whole picture and never moves the path against the rooms. Automatic starts from the turn of the map the robot saved, including one set in the iRobot app, and changes to the angle that puts the robot’s path in the rooms once a run has shown it clearly; the path already drawn turns with it. If the path still runs through walls or beside its rooms, set an angle: the path already drawn turns as soon as you save. |
| **Map size (pixels)** | Map canvas size in pixels (400–1200). Default: 600. |
| **Scale (mm/pixel)** | Millimetres per pixel (5–30). Default 10 = 6 m × 6 m at 600 px. |
| **Floor label (e.g. Ground Floor)** | Free text, for example Ground Floor. Groups robots in the fleet view. |
| **Correlate dirt with sensors (optional)** | Sensors such as humidity or pollen. After 30 missions Roomba+ reports whether the robot collects more dirt when they are high. Calculated locally. |
| **Draw room names on the map image** | Writes each room's name onto the map image. |
| **Create a button for each saved favorite** | One button for each favourite saved in the iRobot app. On a busy account that is a lot of buttons. |
| **Show cleaning schedules as a calendar** | Shows the robot's cleaning schedules as a calendar. |
| **Draw clean zones** | Outlines the clean zones on the map image. |
| **Draw keep-out zones** | Outlines the keep-out zones on the map image. |
| **Draw no-mop zones** | Outlines the no-mop zones on the map image. |
| **Separate sensor per room and zone** | Creates a separate sensor for every room and zone. |
| **Rotate the map picture** | Turns every map picture clockwise as a whole, rooms and path together, for example to match the iRobot app. It never moves the path against the rooms; for that, use “Align the path with the rooms”. The map has no north: its top is the way the robot faced when it left the dock, so it depends on how the dock stands. |
| **Wall thickness (cm)** | How thick walls are drawn on the maps. On a 900-series robot it also decides which two rooms' edges are one wall. Default 15. |
| **Door width (cm)** | How wide a door is drawn on the maps; an opening clearly wider is drawn as an open passage. A Smart Map robot also looks for doors of about this width when it lines its path up with its rooms. Default 80. |
| **Send an ignored command once more** | If the robot accepts a start, room or zone command and no mission begins, Roomba+ sends it once more. Only when the robot reports no reason for refusing it. |
| **Send home after a pause (minutes)** | A robot that stands paused this long is sent back to its base. 0 turns this off. |

## Manually enter Smart Map zones

*Configure → Manually enter Smart Map zones*

Enter your room region IDs as a comma-separated list (e.g. 5, 12, 7). Find them in the HA diagnostics download under options → discovered_zone_ids, or start a room-specific clean from the iRobot app while HA is connected and check the diagnostics afterwards.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Region IDs (comma-separated)** | Example: 5, 12, 7 |
| **Zone name assignments** | One entry per line: 21=Corridor, 22=Kitchen, etc. |

## Blocking sensors

*Configure → Blocking sensors*

Configure sensors that must be inactive before a smart_start can begin.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Blocking sensors** | Binary sensors that block a start when ON (e.g. door open, motion detected). |
| **Behavior when blocked** | Abort immediately or queue the start until sensors clear. |
| **Queue timeout (minutes)** | How long to wait for sensors to clear before giving up. |

## Edit zone: {zone_name}

*Configure → Zone management (after picking a zone)*

Set a display name and visibility for this zone.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Display name** | Custom name shown in selectors. Leave blank to use the default name. |
| **Hide this zone** | Hidden zones are removed from selectors and will not trigger naming repair issues. |

## Presence-aware scheduling

*Configure → Presence-aware scheduling*

Automatically unfreeze the cleaning schedule when everyone leaves home.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Enable presence-aware scheduling** | Holds cleaning schedules while someone is home and releases them once everyone has left. |
| **Tracked persons** | The people whose presence counts. |
| **Mode** | “Unfreeze when all away” releases schedules automatically; “Fire event (manual control)” leaves the decision to your own automation. |
| **Delay after leaving (minutes)** | How long everyone must be gone before schedules are released. |
| **Delay before second robot start** | An extra wait after the away delay before cleaning actually starts. |

## Demand cleaning

*Configure → Demand cleaning*

Automatically start a clean when the floor is significantly dirtier than usual.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Enable demand cleaning** | Starts a clean automatically when the floor is noticeably dirtier than usual. |
| **Trigger multiplier (e.g. 1.5 = 50% above average)** | How far above the usual dirt level triggers a clean: 1.5 means 50% above average. |

## Demand cleaning

*Configure → Demand cleaning (Prime robots)*

Your robot rates how dirty each room is and says from which value a room needs cleaning. With demand cleaning on, Roomba+ asks after each finished mission and starts the dirtiest room past that value: one room at a time, at most every 6 hours, only with the robot on its dock, and only when presence scheduling and the blocking sensors allow a start.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Enable demand cleaning** | Starts the dirtiest room the robot reports as needing a clean, after a mission ends. |

## Per-room cleaning frequency

*Configure → Cleaning frequency per room*

Set how often each room should be cleaned. 'Learned' keeps the room's own self-calibrated interval from its cleaning history.


## Name detected areas

*Configure → Rooms & zones (robots without a Smart Map)*

{map}



{robot}: these areas from the robot's cleaning runs have no name yet: {zone_ids}. This robot keeps no map of its own, so the areas are Roomba+'s: it divides the floor the robot has covered at its narrow points.



On the map above, each area is a coloured patch with its number, or its name once it has one; the green dot is the dock. The map is drawn from the dock, so it may be turned compared with your floor plan. The field with the same number names the area.



Type a name into the field for each area you want to name, and leave the rest empty. Named areas appear in the “Select zone” list and in the mission history.


## Name rooms

*Configure → Rooms & zones (Smart Map robots)*

{map}



{robot}: these rooms on the robot's map have no name yet: {zone_ids}. The map above shows each one with its number; the field with the same number names it. All other rooms already have their name from your iRobot account.



Type a name into the field for each room you want to name, and leave the rest empty. The names stay in Home Assistant — nothing is renamed in your iRobot account.

*Configure → Import rooms from roomba_rest980*

## Maintenance settings

*Configure → Maintenance → Settings*

How the robot reminds you of maintenance. Repair issues and the calendar are off unless you switch them on.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Show maintenance as a to-do list** | Shows due maintenance as a to-do list. |
| **Cleaning reminders** | Reminds you to clean the filter, brushes, wheels, cliff sensors and charging contacts on iRobot's care calendar. Adds a “next cleaning due” sensor and “cleaned” buttons. Replacement reminders work without it. |
| **Pets in the household** | Reminds you to clean the filter and the main brushes twice a week instead of once, as iRobot recommends for homes with pets. Only with cleaning reminders on. |
| **Report a part as "soon" from** | Share of its interval at which a part counts as soon. iRobot's app warns at 80 %. |
| **Guide when an error points to a care task** | List: an item in the maintenance list while the robot reports the error. Repairs: a repair issue instead. Off: neither. The list option needs the maintenance list on. |
| **Repair issue for a part a week overdue** | One repair issue per part, a week after it became due. Off by default; the maintenance list shows it anyway. |
| **Maintenance calendar** | A read-only calendar with the due dates. It puts the calendar in the sidebar. |
| **Hide the maintenance diagnostic entities** | Disables "last replaced", "wear rate" and "days until due" for every part; their figures stay available as attributes of the part sensors. Dashboards and automations using them stop updating. Switch off to show them again. |
| **Filter interval** | Hours of use between replacements. Empty: automatic (the robot's counter, your own replacements, the series, then iRobot's figure). |
| **Main brushes interval** | Hours of use between replacements. Empty: automatic (the robot's counter, your own replacements, the series, then iRobot's figure). |
| **Side brush interval** | Hours of use between replacements. Empty: automatic (the robot's counter, your own replacements, the series, then iRobot's figure). |
| **Clean Base bag interval** | Hours of use between replacements. Empty: automatic (the robot's counter, your own replacements, the series, then iRobot's figure). |

## Report maintenance done

*Configure → Maintenance → Report a part replaced or a task done*

The same as ticking the item off or the maintenance_done action. On a Prime robot the reset goes to iRobot.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Entry** | The entry to mark done; its current state is in brackets. |
| **Action** | Empty: the entry's own. A part to replace can be reported as only cleaned; its counter stays. |

## Forget learned intervals

*Configure → Maintenance → Forget learned intervals*

Forgets the replacement interval learned from your own replacements -- after a reset pressed by mistake or a part swapped early. The current part's count stays; learning starts again with the next two replacements.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Parts** | Nothing ticked: every part. In brackets: where its interval comes from now. |

## Care guides

*Configure → Maintenance → Care guides*

How to clean or replace each part of this robot, with a drawing of where it is.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Guide** | The guides for this robot's parts and care tasks, those due first. |
